title: PowerShell full-access LSASS handle on scranton (credential dumping / in-memory theft)
rationale: F01, F09, F22 and F41 all describe the same 2020-05-02T03:05:16Z event on scranton where PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, pbeesly) opened lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff and an UNKNOWN call trace; F60 covers the csc.exe Add-Type compilation in the same hidden PowerShell chain that precedes the LSASS access. Best fit is LSASS memory credential dumping (T1003.001); the network-provider and API-hooking framings in F41/F09 are not supported by registry/file evidence.

title: wsmprovhost.exe full-access LSASS handle on nashua
rationale: WinRM host process running as pbeesly opened lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff (VM_READ) from managed code on nashua — LSASS memory credential dumping.

title: sdclt.exe (UAC-bypass binary) launched from cmd.exe on scranton just before the credential-access tooling
rationale: not grouped by the consolidation step

title: Hardcoded plaintext credentials in attacker PowerShell tooling on scranton
rationale: Invoke-Exfil and Get-PrivateKeys scripts embed plaintext credentials ('cozy'/'MyCozyPassw0rd!', 'saribas') — unsecured credentials in tooling.

title: accesschk.exe wrote passwordsDB on scranton
rationale: F26 and F59 cover the same accesschk.exe invocation (03:04:34-35Z) writing C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\passwordsDB — credential material written to a file, i.e. credentials in files.

title: PsExec64 with cleartext domain password from scranton to nashua
rationale: F57 and F58 describe the same PsExec64 command line embedding the plaintext dmevals\pbeesly password used to authenticate to nashua; F51 is the same pbeesly tooling chain on scranton including that PsExec64 cleartext credential. The credential-access-relevant action is the cleartext credential in the command line (T1552.001); the resulting remote execution is lateral movement.

title: Get-PrivateKeys exported machine certificate private keys to password-protected .pfx on scranton
rationale: F25 and F55 describe the same Get-PrivateKeys script block (readme.ps1) enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and calling Export-PfxCertificate to Downloads\<random>.pfx with hardcoded password 'saribas'. This is theft of authentication certificate private keys (T1649), which fits better than the generic private-keys technique.

title: DLLs written to user Temp are Add-Type compilations, not password filter DLLs
rationale: The finding itself concludes these Temp DLLs are PowerShell Add-Type compilations for in-memory code execution, not LSA notification packages; no password-filter modification occurred, so this is not credential access.

title: WebDAV cookie creation (DavSetCookie) on scranton
rationale: DavSetCookie/INetCookies artifacts are the WebDAV client storing an auth cookie for the exfil share; this is ingress-tool transfer/exfil channel use, not forged web session credentials.

title: hostui.lnk dropped into all-users StartUp folder on scranton
rationale: The finding describes a shortcut dropped into the StartUp folder and later run with -verb runas — persistence/elevation, not forced authentication.
